summary.brief: A man shows how to remove corroded freeze (expansion) plugs, clean the holes, and install new plugs on a car engine.
summary.detailed: The video begins with title cards introducing a tutorial on replacing freeze plugs. A man wearing a black short‑sleeved shirt stands beside a red car with the hood raised and points out rust‑corroded rubber expansion plugs on the engine block. He displays an expansion‑plug set with a swivel‑head driver and selects the size that matches each plug. Using the driver (and a hammer when needed) he extracts the old, corroded plugs from their threaded holes. He then cleans each hole by sanding the outer edge and rubbing the interior with a piece of memory cloth to remove rust and debris. After the holes are clear, he drives the new plugs into place, keeping them square with the swivel‑head tool and, for tighter locations, using a red electric drill to assist. The steps—removal, cleaning, and installation—are shown in fast‑motion for each plug until the job is finished, followed by a thank‑you screen.

action.detailed: Extract the corroded freeze plugs with the swivel‑head driver, clean each hole with sand and a memory‑cloth rag, then drive new plugs into the engine block squarely using the same driver and a power drill for hard‑to‑reach plugs.
action.actor: A man in a black short‑sleeved shirt standing beside a red car with its hood open

summary.brief: The man extracts the corroded freeze plugs from the engine using an expansion‑plug tool and cleans each opening.
